display_name: Birth a solet from an existing GitHub genesis clone
description: MidwifeServiceInterface implementation for the GitHub-sourced genesis axis: born from a seed clone with no parent filesystem copy, as opposed to macos_midwife_plugin's copy-from-a-running-parent axis. environment_config['target'] is REQUIRED and MUST be an EXISTING, fully-formed platform clone (ananta/ + plugins/ present -- knowledge_bases/ is NOT required: a seed-born clone ships without it and genesis's materialize_kb_symlinks step creates it), for example a seed folder produced by assemble_seed. Genesis runs against it directly (existing-clone mode). Acquisition mode -- cloning a pinned upstream into an absent/empty target -- was RETIRED: the Seed Factory replaces it, so an absent/empty target raises a validation error (assemble a seed into it first). The optional provision_venv flag selects the birth VARIANT for the local-birth chain (the mint_and_birth_local joseki): when True, birth runs create_venv_and_install_seed EXPLICITLY and UNCONDITIONALLY before genesis, because an assembled seed folder ships source-only (no .venv); when False (default), the standard existing-clone contract is unchanged and genesis assumes a pre-existing <target>/.venv (fail-loud if absent). The flow: profile-driven allowlist install, then the 6-step spine (validate_name / resolve_target / materialize_configs / seed_root_manifest / materialize_kb_symlinks / write_manifest_marker), then credential seeding, first-boot vault passphrase file seed, and LaunchAgent autostart install (which also performs the first launch via launchd RunAtLoad semantics). Credential contract (per-solet DB-role isolation, operator override): every solet has its OWN non-superuser Postgres role and database, both named after it. The newborn's db, pgvector extension, role, and localhost scram gate are created by WIZARD STEP 1 -- an agent-run pre-launch step the driving agent performs with runbook guidance -- and genesis ASSUMES them, verifying the one invisible failure mode with a pre-seed NEGATIVE auth probe (a wrong password reaching the newborn's db means scram is not gating it: refuse loud). The newborn then SELF-SEEDS its own role: a subprocess in the newborn's OWN venv (SOLET_NAME=<newborn>) generates a fresh password, stores it in the newborn's own Keychain namespace (both owner-plugin keys), ALTER ROLEs the newborn's own role, and finally proves isolation -- its role must be REFUSED CONNECT on the birthing parent's database (the R4 PUBLIC revoke). No credential ever crosses a solet namespace; there is no parent-provisions-child copy and no shared cluster role. The verb therefore requires SOLET_NAME to be set in the birthing (parent) process -- it names the sibling database the isolation proof runs against. A target that is absent/empty or is not a valid clone raises a validation error immediately, before any state is touched -- this verb never guesses or clobbers a directory. dry_run=True returns a planned BirthResult (message names the resolved existing-clone target and whether the venv would be provisioned) without mutating filesystem/Postgres/venv/launchd state. The verb is sync and NOT idempotent-by-tag (unlike the AWS/macOS midwife siblings) -- re-running against the same target re-runs every step, each of which is independently idempotent (probe-first, skip-if-already-healthy) at the underlying-slice level.
embedding_description: Birth a new solet from an existing platform clone on disk, such as a seed folder produced by the seed factory: run genesis against that directory so it becomes a live, self-standing solet with its own identity. Local birth, with an option to provision the seed folder's virtual environment first. The newborn seeds its own database credential in its own namespace.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: BirthResult frozen dataclass with status (success / failed / dry_run -- 'partial' is not currently emitted by this implementation), solet_name, idempotency_key (sha256 of name+profile_template+environment_config, informational -- not currently used for resume), dry_run echo, steps audit tuple (the 6-step spine records: validate_name/resolve_target/materialize_configs/seed_root_manifest/materialize_kb_symlinks/write_manifest_marker, each with step_name+status+optional error/detail fields -- empty on a failure that occurs BEFORE the spine runs, e.g. a provision_venv venv/install failure), manifest_path of the per-genesis attempt-marker JSON (the on-disk marker additionally records the post-spine phases credential_seed / vault_passphrase / install_autostart and carries the final success/failed status -- a marker still reading 'spine_complete' means genesis died mid-phases), iam_roles_created (always empty -- no AWS/IAM), rds_endpoint (always empty -- local Postgres), kms_key_arn (always empty -- no KMS), and a human-readable message.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with status. On status='success', surface solet_name and manifest_path so the operator can audit what genesis did. On status='failed', surface message verbatim -- it already names which underlying step or stage failed and why (the provision_venv venv/install runs BEFORE the 6-step spine, so a failure there means steps is empty; otherwise: profile-driven allowlist install / the 6-step spine / the pre-seed scram verify / the newborn credential self-seed / autostart install). On status='dry_run', state that nothing was mutated, and surface the target directory and whether the venv would have been provisioned.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: On success the solet is birthed and its LaunchAgent performs first launch; the driving agent's next steps are the seed hydration runbook (operator launch tooling, MCP bridge registration). On a failed BirthResult, do NOT re-birth blindly -- read the message, fix the named cause (commonly an incomplete WIZARD STEP 1), and re-run against the same target (every underlying slice is idempotent).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Birth a solet from an existing GitHub genesis clone (existing-clone mode; optional provision_venv variant for source-only seed folders).
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_name / missing_profile_template: required top-level arguments not supplied. invalid_environment_config: environment_config is missing the required 'target' key entirely, OR 'target' is absent/empty (NOT birthable -- acquisition-mode clone-of-pinned-upstream was retired; assemble a seed into it first), OR 'target' points at a non-empty directory that is not a fully-formed platform clone (missing ananta/ or plugins/) -- this verb refuses to guess or clobber. birth_solet_crashed: an unexpected exception during genesis (surfaces the exception message verbatim). Step-level failures inside a 'failed' BirthResult (not a raised exception) name the failing stage directly: provision_venv-only failures -- 'venv creation failed' / 'build-backend install (pip/setuptools/wheel) failed' / 'seed install failed for <package>' (a pip/venv issue while building the source-only seed folder's venv); shared by all births -- 'SOLET_NAME is not set in the birthing (parent) process' (the verb cannot determine the sibling database the newborn must prove isolation from), 'database <name> accepts role <name> with a WRONG password -- it is passwordless-accessible' (the pre-seed negative-auth probe found the localhost scram gate missing: wizard step 1's R3 default-scram lines were never inserted, or pg_reload_conf was not run), 'newborn credential self-seed subprocess exited <n>: <stderr tail>' (the newborn's own-venv self-seed failed -- the surfaced stderr tail is secret-free by construction and names the actionable cause, e.g. the newborn's role does not exist yet (wizard step 1 not run) or the post-seed isolation proof found the newborn's role could reach the parent's database (the R4 PUBLIC revoke is missing on the parent's db)), 'profile-driven allowlist install failed' (an allowlisted plugin's pyproject.toml is missing or pip failed), 'genesis step machine failed at validate_name' (name does not match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,62}), 'genesis step machine failed at resolve_target' (the target directory does not look like a full platform clone), 'genesis step machine failed at materialize_configs' (a materialize-time fail-loud verification: the postgres connect-user did not resolve to the newborn's own role, or the default_knowledge_plugin knowledge_base_root injection is missing/clobbered), 'autostart install failed' (launchctl issue).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: missing args: re-issue with name + profile_template populated. invalid_environment_config: point environment_config['target'] at an EXISTING full clone of the platform repo (ananta/ + plugins/ present) -- most commonly a seed folder produced by assemble_seed; an absent/empty target is no longer acquired for you (assemble a seed first), and this verb never accepts a caller-supplied source repo or clone URL. provision_venv failures: a venv/install failure is typically transient (network, disk, pip index) -- re-run against the same target (the failed attempt leaves the folder as a still-source-only clone). SOLET_NAME-not-set: export the PARENT's own name in the birthing process before invoking the verb. Pre-seed scram-verify or self-seed failures point at WIZARD STEP 1 -- the agent-run pre-launch provisioning the hydration runbook prescribes: createuser (plain, non-superuser) the newborn's role, createdb -O owned by it, CREATE EXTENSION vector, REVOKE CONNECT, TEMP ... FROM PUBLIC (R4), and on the machine's first newborn insert the R3 default-scram pg_hba block + pg_reload_conf; complete/repair that step, then re-run the verb. An isolation-proof failure (newborn can reach the parent's db) means the R4 revoke is missing on the PARENT's database -- apply it there. resolve_target failures: confirm the target directory is a genuine platform clone (a seed folder or a git clone), not a partial/wrong directory. Step failures inside profile-driven allowlist install or the credential self-seed: re-run -- every underlying slice is independently idempotent (probe-first, skip-if-healthy), so a re-run resumes cleanly rather than duplicating work. autostart install failures: check the message for a launchctl observation failure (distinct from a legitimate not-loaded state) versus an actual load/unload failure; a stale LaunchAgent from a prior partial attempt is handled automatically (unload-before-reload) once the underlying launchctl probe itself can observe state cleanly.
